title.narrative: Life-Saving Inclusive Integrated Nutrition and Protection Lean Season response for community resilience to Conflict-Affected population in Borno.

description.narrative: ltpgtBuilding on the critical progress realized through previous NHF-supported interventions including the 2023 Standard Allocation, 2023 Reserve Allocation, and the 2024 Third Reserve Allocation, theltbgt Future Resilience and Development Foundationlt/bgt (FRAD Foundation), in consortium with the ltbgtElela-Care Humanitarian Development Organizationlt/bgt (ECM) and ltbgt Roadmap for Women and Youth Development (RAWYOD) ,lt/bgt proposes a comprehensive and inclusive six-month humanitarian response in Borno.lt/pgtltpgtThis intervention seeks to address life-threatening levels of acute malnutrition, gender-based violence (GBV) affecting IDPs, returnees and host communities in Borno State during lean season. The proposed project aligns with the objectives of the 2025 First Standard Allocation strategy, which is "Addressing Immediate Food Insecurity in North-East Nigeria" by targeting two priority LGAs experiencing crisis and emergency food insecurity (IPC Phase 4): Magumeri (FRAD,ECM RAWYOD), Mobbar (FRAD) in Borno state.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe consortium will deploy its qualified staff to address and respond to the needs in the aforementioned LGAs in the following components.lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtltbgt1. Nutritionlt/bgtltbrgtThe intervention adopts an integrated, community-based nutrition response that prioritizes the treatment of Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM) using the culturally adapted TSFP using Tom Brown approach and Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) without medical complication through Outpatient Therapeutic Programs (OTP) using RUTF while referral are made for cases with medical complications to the stabilization centers Managed by Intersos in Magumeri and ACF in Mobbar LGA. Preventive activities will address underlying determinants of malnutrition, including food insecurity, recurrent flooding, and disease outbreaks. Community nutrition mobilizers (CNMs) will be trained and deployed to improve outreach and early identification of malnutrition.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtltbgt2. GBV Responselt/bgtltbrgtThe project will deliver a robust protection package for women, girls, this include GBV case management, Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS), Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA), and the provision of dignity kits. Women and Girls Safe Spaces (WGSS) will offer life skills training and livelihood support. The response will integrate protection mainstreaming principles, ensuring accountability to affected populations and adherence to Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) standards. Additionally the project will contribute to the GBV sector referral mechanism to ensure wider support to the affected population. FRAD will leverage on existing partners for linkages in the implementation LGAs.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtBuilding on NHF priority for inclusion in humanitarian response, disability Inclusion and Community Empowerment will be a top priority of the response strategy, the consortium will emphasize meaningful inclusion of persons with disabilities particularly women and children by embedding inclusive practices across all intervention sectors. FRAD will lead the consortium initiative ensuring other cross cutting issues like gender, AAP, PSEA and protection are mainstreamed.lt/pgtltpgt lt/pgtltpgtltspangtThe consortium will implement a robust MEAL framework, including baseline and end-line assessments, monthly supportive supervision, joint monitoring visits, bi-monthly senior-level oversight, and quarterly project review meetings. lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltspangtltbrgtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltspangtltbgtTheory of Changelt/bgtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltspangtltbgtltbrgtlt/bgtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltbgtIf lt/bgtltbrgtVulnerable populations in high-priority LGAs receive integrated nutrition and protection services that is inclusive ltbgtAND lt/bgtInterventions are monitored in real time providing needed supportltbrgtltbgtThenlt/bgtltbrgtComprehensive Services (Acute malnutrition, protection risks, and gender-based violence) risk will be reduced, leading to improved safety, and resilience among women, children, and persons with disabilities during the lean season.ltbrgtlt/pgt
